newsitem.title: USA: CBOT members to vote on new delivery locations.
newsitem.headline: CBOT members to vote on new delivery locations.

text.p: Chicago Board of Trade members will vote on April 15 on a proposal to add new grain delivery locations along the northern Illinois River, the CBOT said.

"The Board of Directors of the Chicago Board of Trade, acting on a unanimous recommendation by the Grain Delivery Task Force, today voted to send a proposal for new delivery terms for corn and soybeans to the CBOT membership for a ballot vote," the exchange said.
The new locations would be along the northern Illinois River from Pekin, Illinois, to Chicago, including Burns Harbor, Indiana.
CBOT Chairman Pat Arbor said he would hold a floor meeting to discuss the proposal on April 1.
The members in October rejected a similar plan to expand the number of delivery locations.
The second proposal comes after the Commodity Futures Trading Commission ordered the CBOT to resolve the exchange's shortage of grain storage space.
CFTC said in December the exchange had 75 days to resolve the storage capacity shortage or the government agency would formulate its own solution.
One analyst said, "I think it's pretty clear if they voted not to do something, CFTC would do it for them."
